evals.prompt: I have a staged auth change that adds SMS fallback to the login flow. Please generate and execute one Conventional Commit for it, and keep emoji enabled.
evals.expected_output: Treat it as a single-feature commit and produce or execute an English feat(auth) style commit with emoji, without pushing.
assertions: Header is a single feat commit with scope auth
Emoji is retained in the header
Output language is English (request is English)
Does not run git push

evals.prompt: The staged set mixes an order-service bug fix and a README update. Do not commit yet. Tell me whether it should split into two commits and draft both headers.
evals.expected_output: Prefer a split plan and English candidate headers instead of merging the mixed staged set into one vague commit.
assertions: Recommends splitting into two commits
Drafts a fix header and a docs header separately
Does not merge the mixed set into one vague commit
Does not execute git commit

evals.prompt: This change reshapes the /api/user/profile response and removes the old fields. Generate the commit message and mark it as a breaking change.
evals.expected_output: The header may include ! and the footer should include a BREAKING CHANGE note, with English scope/subject/body.
assertions: Marks the breaking change via ! in the header and/or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer
Body or footer explains the migration impact, not just 'breaking'
Output language is English

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for fixing duplicate ledger writes in the payment callback, close #128, reference #130, and include Jira PROJ-456.
evals.expected_output: Correctly distinguish Closes #128, Refs #130, and an extra footer line such as Jira: PROJ-456.
assertions: Closes #128 appears in the footer
Refs #130 appears in the footer and is NOT written as Closes
Jira PROJ-456 is rendered as a footer/trailer line
Header type is fix

evals.prompt: There are no staged changes in the repo, but I want to commit now. What should you do under this skill?
evals.expected_output: Stop clearly and tell the user to stage files first instead of inventing a commit or running git commit anyway.
assertions: Stops and tells the user to stage files first
Does not invent a commit or run git commit

evals.prompt: Do not actually commit. Draft a commit message for fixing the virtualized list performance issue. Do not include any Co-Authored-By line.
evals.expected_output: Draft only, do not run git commit, and do not include Co-Authored-By or attribution lines.
assertions: Returns a draft only and does not run git commit
No Co-Authored-By line
No AI attribution line such as 'Generated with Claude Code'

evals.prompt: 请使用中文拆分提交所有的改动。当前没有 staged，另外还有两个未跟踪文件。先判断应该拆成几个 commit，再按方案执行。
evals.expected_output: Enter all-changes mode and chinese-output together (the explicit phrase forces Chinese), plan the split against the full staged/unstaged/untracked set, and use Chinese for the resulting commit text or split plan.
assertions: Enters all-changes mode (includes untracked files in the candidate set)
Output language is Chinese
Plans the split against the full working-tree change set before executing

evals.prompt: 当前没有 staged，但我要把所有改动直接提交，包括新文件。请生成并执行一个 Conventional Commit。
evals.expected_output: Enter all-changes mode without asking the user to stage files manually first. Because the request itself is written in Chinese, the auto-detected commit-language is Chinese — the commit text should be Chinese even though the legacy magic phrase was not used.
assertions: Enters all-changes mode without asking the user to stage files manually first
Auto-detects the commit-language as Chinese from the Chinese request
Produces a Chinese subject (does NOT fall back to English just because the legacy phrase was absent)

evals.prompt: Split and commit all changes, but one file mixes two unrelated purposes. Handle it directly.
evals.expected_output: Recognize all-changes mode, but stop at the split-plan layer because the split would require hunk-level surgery inside one file.
assertions: Recognizes all-changes mode
Stops at the split-plan layer instead of committing
Reason given is that a clean split would require hunk-level surgery inside one file

evals.prompt: I have a staged auth change that adds SMS fallback to the login flow. Please commit it. Use agent-mode defaults.
evals.expected_output: Header has emoji and no [AI] tag. Body starts with a Why: line. Trailers include Agent-Task, Agent-Model matching the running model id, and Generated-By: agent. Local git commit -F only. No Co-authored-by, Made-with, or Committed via line.
assertions: Header has an emoji and does NOT contain the [AI] tag
Body starts with a Why: line explaining the motivation
Trailers include Agent-Task, Agent-Model, and Generated-By: agent
Uses local git commit -F, not GitHub web/API
No Co-authored-by, Made-with, or Committed via line

evals.prompt: I'm midway through refactoring refresh token rotation. Just give me a checkpoint commit so I don't lose progress. Don't worry about polishing the message.
evals.expected_output: Recognize checkpoint-mode. Produce a single chore(wip) checkpoint commit with a [WIP] marker and no [AI] tag. Skip the Why-line requirement. Still attach Agent-Task / Agent-Model / Generated-By trailers. Remind the user to squash [WIP] commits before merging.
assertions: Produces a single chore(wip) commit with a [WIP] marker and no [AI] tag
Skips the Why-line requirement
Still attaches Agent-Task / Agent-Model / Generated-By trailers
Reminds the user to squash [WIP] commits before merging

evals.prompt: Commit my staged bug fix to the cart total calculator. Don't add any AI tag or agent trailer — I want a normal Conventional Commit.
evals.expected_output: Disable agent-mode. Header has no [AI] tag, no Agent-* / Generated-By trailers. Standard Conventional Commit with emoji preserved.
assertions: Header has no [AI] tag
No Agent-Task / Agent-Model / Agent-Prompt-Ref / Generated-By trailers
Standard Conventional Commit with emoji preserved

evals.prompt: Commit this staged feat change. The diff modifies the user profile API but I haven't said why I'm doing it.
evals.expected_output: Type is feat, Why is required. Since the agent cannot infer a real motivation from the diff alone, stop and ask the user to supply the Why before composing. Do not fabricate a Why line and do not run git commit.
assertions: Identifies that Why is required for a feat commit
Stops and asks the user to supply the Why
Does not fabricate a Why line and does not run git commit

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for fixing duplicate ledger writes in the payment callback, close #128, and link it to task tracker URL https://linear.app/x/issue/PAY-77.
evals.expected_output: Closes #128 stays in the standard footer. The task tracker URL is rendered as Agent-Task: https://linear.app/x/issue/PAY-77, not mixed into Closes. Agent-Model and Generated-By trailers attach. Header includes a fix emoji, no [AI] tag, and the body has a Why line.
assertions: Closes #128 stays in the standard footer
The Linear URL is rendered as Agent-Task:, not mixed into Closes
Agent-Model and Generated-By trailers attach
Header includes a fix emoji and no [AI] tag, and the body has a Why line

evals.prompt: 把我暂存的购物车总价修复提交了，这个 bug 是删除商品后总价没刷新。
evals.expected_output: The request is written in Chinese with no magic phrase, so the auto-detected commit-language is Chinese. Produce and execute a fix(cart) commit with a Chinese subject, emoji, no [AI] tag, a Why line, plus agent trailers.
assertions: Auto-detects the commit-language as Chinese from the request (no legacy magic phrase needed)
Header is a fix commit with emoji and no [AI] tag
Subject and Why line are written in Chinese

evals.prompt: Commit my staged change. Match whatever language this project usually uses — its recent commits all look like 'feat(动态工作流): 收紧编排触发并补齐脚手架验证'.
evals.expected_output: With no explicit language instruction and a language-neutral request, the skill should fall through to repo-history detection and match the project's Chinese commit habit.
assertions: Samples or honors the repository's commit history to decide language
Produces a Chinese subject to match the repo's existing style

evals.prompt: Commit my staged auth fix for the SMS retry bug. I verified it with `just ci`, I'm confident it's correct, and the blast radius is narrow.
evals.expected_output: Produce a fix(auth) commit in agent-mode with the quality-trail trailers filled in: Tested: just ci, Confidence: high, Scope-risk: narrow, ordered before the Agent-* trailers.
assertions: Includes a Tested: just ci trailer
Includes Confidence and Scope-risk trailers reflecting the user's statement
Quality trailers are ordered before Agent-Task / Agent-Model / Generated-By

evals.prompt: Commit my staged change with this exact subject: 添加短信兜底登录并重构验证码服务与限流降级回退到备用通道的完整逻辑
evals.expected_output: That subject is far wider than 72 display columns. The skill should keep the header within ~72 columns (tighten the subject) and move the extra detail into the body, rather than forcing an overlong header through.
assertions: Final commit header is within roughly 72 display columns
Overflow detail is moved into the body rather than left in a giant subject line

evals.prompt: Stage and commit everything — I added a new login feature plus a .env file with the production API keys.
evals.expected_output: The preflight safety scan should flag the .env secret, refuse to commit it silently, and ask the user to confirm or unstage it before proceeding.
assertions: Flags the .env / secret file during preflight
Does not silently commit the secret into history
Asks the user to confirm or unstage the secret before proceeding

evals.prompt: Commit my staged change. Heads up: this repo has a pre-commit hook that reformats files and aborts the commit when it rewrites anything.
evals.expected_output: The first commit attempt is aborted by the formatter hook. The skill should re-inspect git status, re-stage the hook's edits, retry the same commit message, and attribute the reformatting to the hook rather than treating it as its own change.
assertions: Re-inspects git status after the hook aborts the commit
Re-stages the hook's edits and retries the same commit message
Reports that the hook reformatted files instead of claiming the change as its own
Does not rewrite the commit message in response to the formatter abort

evals.prompt: Commit my staged docs update. Note: this repo's commitlint config only allows types [feat, fix, docs, chore], forbids emoji, and caps the header at 60 characters.
evals.expected_output: Repo config is authoritative over the skill's defaults: pick an allowed type, omit emoji even though the skill defaults to emoji-on, and keep the header within 60 characters.
assertions: Treats the commitlint config as authoritative over the skill's defaults
Omits emoji from the header
Header stays within the configured 60-character limit
Uses the docs type from the allowed list

evals.prompt: 请使用中文拆分提交所有的改动，使用 emoji，然后按方案执行提交；不要 push。当前变更已经确认是一个原子版本同步提交，没有 secret 或大文件。
evals.expected_output: Because the user explicitly authorized execution and no safety gate is tripped, the skill should show the final message/file set for transparency and then run the local commit without asking for an extra ok/confirmation. It must still avoid pushing.
assertions: Treats the request as execution-authorized instead of waiting for an extra ok
Displays the final commit message and file set before committing
Runs the local commit when the split is safe and no safety gate is tripped
Does not run git push

evals.prompt: 请使用中文拆分提交所有的改动，使用 emoji。当前除了源码改动，还有未跟踪的 output/demo-recording.mp4（180MB）和 cache/model.bin（85MB）。有些大文件可能应该加到 .gitignore，不要全都提交。
evals.expected_output: Enter all-changes mode, but stop at the safety gate because large untracked files are present. The skill should list each large file, avoid git add -A, ask for a per-file decision, and propose .gitignore patterns for generated/cache artifacts when appropriate.
assertions: Detects the large untracked files during preflight
Does not run git add -A or commit all large files silently
Asks for a per-file include / ignore / leave-local decision
Suggests .gitignore patterns for generated or cache artifacts when appropriate
Keeps output language Chinese

evals.prompt: Commit my staged refactor. This repo's commitlint config sets header-max-length to 100, and the natural subject is about 85 columns wide.
evals.expected_output: Repo config is authoritative over the skill's 72-column default: keep the ~85-column header and pass the relaxed limit to the compose script via --max-header-width 100 instead of truncating a legal subject.
assertions: Treats the repo's 100-column commitlint limit as authoritative over the skill's default 72
Passes --max-header-width 100 (or equivalent) to the compose script rather than shortening the subject to fit 72
Does not reject or truncate the ~85-column header

evals.prompt: Commit my staged emergency production patch. This repo's commitlint type-enum is [feat, fix, hotfix, docs, chore] and its history uses hotfix for urgent patches exactly like this one.
evals.expected_output: Adopt the repo's custom hotfix type instead of downgrading to fix, and handle the missing built-in emoji explicitly: pass --emoji when emoji fits the repo style, or accept the no-emoji output otherwise.
assertions: Uses the repo's custom hotfix type instead of falling back to fix
Handles the missing built-in emoji explicitly (passes --emoji or accepts the no-emoji output)
Does not claim the composer only supports the 11 built-in types

evals.prompt: Commit my staged change. This repo's CONTRIBUTING says AI-assisted commits must carry an Assisted-by: trailer naming the model, and contributors certify DCO with Signed-off-by.
evals.expected_output: Follow the repo's attribution convention: emit an Assisted-by: trailer via --footer-line, omit the skill's private Agent-* / Generated-By trailer group to avoid double attribution, and never add Signed-off-by itself — DCO sign-off belongs to the human (suggest git commit -s).
assertions: Emits the repo's Assisted-by: trailer naming the model (via --footer-line or equivalent)
Omits the private Agent-Task / Agent-Model / Generated-By trailer group to avoid double attribution
Does not add Signed-off-by itself; points the user at git commit -s for the DCO sign-off

evals.prompt: Commit my staged docs change. Use local git. Do not create the commit on GitHub.com, do not add Committed via Cursor Agent, and do not put [AI] in the subject.
evals.expected_output: Execute with local git commit -F only. Header has no [AI] tag. Message has no Co-authored-by, Made-with, or Committed via line. Does not use GitHub web, Contents API, GraphQL createCommitOnBranch, or MCP push_files / create_or_update_file.
assertions: Uses local git commit -F (or rtk git commit -F) and does not use GitHub web/API/MCP file-commit tools
Header has no [AI] tag
No Co-authored-by, Made-with, or Committed via line in the message
Does not pass git commit --trailer for those keys

evals.prompt: Commit my staged feat. Please add the [AI] tag to the header.
evals.expected_output: User opted in, so pass --ai. Header contains [AI] after the colon and before emoji. Still uses local git commit -F and still omits Co-authored-by / Made-with / Committed via.
assertions: Header contains the [AI] tag because the user opted in
Uses local git commit -F
No Co-authored-by, Made-with, or Committed via line

evals.prompt: 请提交已暂存的购物车总价修复，push 到 origin 的当前分支，再向同一仓库的 main 创建 PR。不要包含未暂存改动。
evals.expected_output: Verify the staged-only local commit, then hand the already-authorized push and PR creation to the main coordinator for gh-pr-release or the appropriate workflow in the same request.
assertions: Uses local git commit only and excludes unstaged changes
Hands off repository, branch, created SHA(s), final HEAD, verification results, ordered remaining actions, and known remote/base targets
Continues the authorized push and PR workflow without treating them as the end of an out-of-scope request or asking for the same authorization again
Preserves receiving-workflow target and exact-head checks

evals.prompt: 提交并 push，再创建 PR。本地 git commit 已被 pre-commit hook 以 lint 错误拒绝，退出码为 1，没有生成新提交。
evals.expected_output: Report the hook rejection and the unfinished commit, push, and PR steps; do not execute dependent remote actions or bypass the failure through GitHub commit APIs.
assertions: Reports the original hook failure and does not claim commit success
Does not execute push or PR steps that depend on the failed commit
Does not create a replacement commit through GitHub web or file-commit APIs

evals.prompt: 提交并 push，再创建 PR。本地提交已成功且完成验证，远程目标也明确，但当前环境没有可用的网络连接或远程操作工具。
evals.expected_output: Return the verified local commit evidence and identify push and PR creation as unfinished due to unavailable remote access.
assertions: Reports the repository, branch, verified commit SHA, and verification results
Names the unavailable continuation capability and remaining push/PR actions
Does not claim the entire request is complete or invent remote success

evals.prompt: 请提交已暂存的修复并 push，再创建 PR。仓库有两个不同的远程目标且没有 upstream；请求和仓库上下文都没有说明要用哪个。
evals.expected_output: Complete the safe local commit and verification, then ask only for the unresolved remote target before executing dependent remote steps.
assertions: Keeps safe authorized local work moving and records the verified SHA
Clarifies the missing target without repeating the already-given commit/push/PR authorization
Does not guess a remote destination
